vuln.description: vsftpd 2.3.4 contains a backdoor triggered by a smiley face in the username field (USER :)) which opens a shell on port 6200.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected vsftpd 2.3.4 running on port 21/tcp
vuln.remediation: Upgrade to vsftpd 2.3.5 or later. Remove the compromised binary.

vuln.description: OpenSSH 4.7p1 uses weak cryptographic algorithms susceptible to CBC mode attacks.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected OpenSSH 4.7p1 running on port 22/tcp
vuln.remediation: Upgrade to OpenSSH 8.x or later and disable weak ciphers.

vuln.description: Apache 2.2.8 is vulnerable to a byte-range DoS attack via crafted Range headers.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected Apache httpd 2.2.8 running on port 80/tcp
vuln.remediation: Upgrade to Apache 2.2.21 or later. Apply vendor patch.

vuln.category: Remote Code Execution — Username Map Script
vuln.description: Samba 3.0.20 allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands by sending shell metacharacters in the username during authentication.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected Samba 3.0.20 on ports 139 and 445
vuln.remediation: Upgrade Samba to >= 3.0.25. Disable the username map script option.

vuln.category: Remote Code Execution — Username Map Script
vuln.description: Samba 3.0.20 allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands by sending shell metacharacters in the username during authentication.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected Samba 3.0.20 on ports 139 and 445
vuln.remediation: Upgrade Samba to >= 3.0.25. Disable the username map script option.

vuln.description: MySQL 5.0.51 has no root password set by default, allowing unauthenticated access.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected MySQL 5.0.51 running on port 3306/tcp
vuln.remediation: Set a strong root password. Restrict remote MySQL access via firewall rules.

report.executive_summary: The penetration test conducted on 192.168.56.101/32 revealed significant security risks. The overall risk level is Critical, with multiple vulnerabilities allowing remote code execution, denial of service, and unauthorized access. The most critical findings include vulnerabilities in vsftpd, Samba, and MySQL, which can be exploited to gain control of the system or disrupt its operation. The most important remediation priority is to upgrade the vulnerable software, including vsftpd, Samba, and MySQL, to the latest versions and apply vendor patches. Additionally, setting a strong root password for MySQL and restricting remote access via firewall rules is essential. The test also identified open web paths, including /phpMyAdmin, /dvwa, and /mutillidae, which may pose additional risks if not properly secured.
report.scope_and_methodology: The penetration test was conducted on 192.168.56.101/32, with a scope of scanning all ports from 1 to 65535. The test used various tools, including nmap, to identify open ports and detect services running on them. No exploitation, login attempts, file modification, or shellcode injection was performed during the test. The test aimed to identify potential vulnerabilities and provide recommendations for remediation without causing any harm to the system.
